WHY THIS EXISTS
A parity wave that only checks pixels will hand an agent a screen whose data
source does not exist. The agent then has two bad options: stall, or invent
the data. Inventing it violates the no-mock-data policy and produces a screen
that demos beautifully and is a lie. This file makes the third option
possible: BUILD THE BACKEND FIRST, or ship the honest unavailable state.
backend values:
ready    — every table / RPC / function the surface needs is deployed.
partial  — some of it exists; the named gap is what blocks completion.
MISSING  — the surface has NO persistence or execution path at all.
degraded — deployed but known non-functional (see note).
wave_action is what a dev agent should DO when it picks this surface up:
build-ui        — backend is ready; implement the screen.
build-backend   — a backend agent must land the schema/function FIRST.
ui+offline      — build the UI, but the empty/unavailable state is the
shipping state until the backend exists. Do NOT synthesize.
blocked         — do not start; an external dependency is broken.
